passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: It is from the past that they have tried to learn, and the past is a pathway which the feet of spirits have trodden and made luminous.

tr.fr: C'est du passé qu'ils ont essayé d'apprendre, et le passé est un chemin que les pieds des esprits ont parcouru et rendu lumineux.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: The effect of education upon the minds of the people was well known to the good Emperors of old.

tr.fr: L’effet de l’éducation sur l’esprit du peuple était bien connu des bons empereurs d’autrefois.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: When parents have a son born to them, the regular line of descent in the family is thereby secured.

tr.fr: Lorsque les parents ont un fils, la lignée régulière de la famille est ainsi assurée.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: When an Emperor can live in harmony with his elders, there will be harmony throughout his dominion between superiors and inferiors; and when he is filial to the Supreme Father and Mother, he will be blessed by them.

tr.fr: Lorsqu'un empereur peut vivre en harmonie avec ses aînés, il y aura harmonie dans toute sa domination entre supérieurs et inférieurs ; et lorsqu'il sera filial envers le Père et la Mère Suprêmes, il sera béni par eux.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: By doing so we shall have performed the duty of mankind, and have done what ought to be done by a filial son, and by the living to the dead.

tr.fr: Ce faisant, nous aurons accompli le devoir de l'humanité et aurons fait ce qui devrait être fait par un fils filial et par un vivant envers les morts.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: He had entered the dense fog on the hills and did not know where he was, when his mother leaned against the door-post and gnawed her fingers as if she would go in quest of him.

tr.fr: Il était entré dans le brouillard épais des collines et ne savait pas où il était, lorsque sa mère s'appuya contre le montant de la porte et se mordit les doigts comme si elle voulait aller à sa recherche.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: In the country of Ch‘u lived Lao Lai Tzŭ, who, when so old that he had lost nearly all his teeth, made every effort to rejoice and comfort his parents, constantly endeavouring to gladden their hearts.

tr.fr: Dans le pays de Chu vivait Lao Lai Tzu, qui, si vieux qu'il avait perdu presque toutes ses dents, faisait tous ses efforts pour réjouir et réconforter ses parents, s'efforçant constamment de réjouir leurs cœurs.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: He was employed in the severest toil, and served his father with entire obedience.

tr.fr: Il était employé aux travaux les plus durs et servait son père avec une entière obéissance.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: He now reveres them, although dead, as if they were alive; and hopes they will condescend to dwell in his ancestral hall.

tr.fr: Il les vénère maintenant, bien que morts, comme s'ils étaient vivants ;  et espère qu'ils daigneront habiter dans sa salle ancestrale.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: Taking up his rice and flesh, Ts‘ai returned home to his mother with the food; and in their joy they even forgot that the year was one of dearth.

tr.fr: Prenant son riz et sa chair, Ts'ai rentra chez sa mère avec la nourriture ;  et dans leur joie, ils oubliaient même que c'était une année de disette.

passages.w: The book of filial duty
passages.s: His mother was in the habit of eating fresh fish at her meals, but winter coming, the ice bound up the rivers.

tr.fr: Sa mère avait l'habitude de manger du poisson frais à ses repas, mais l'hiver venu, les glaces bloquaient les rivières.

formulas.text: It is from the past that they have tried to learn, and the past is a pathway which the feet of spirits have trodden and made luminous.

When an Emperor can live in harmony with his elders, there will be harmony throughout his dominion between superiors and inferiors; and when he is filial to the Supreme Father and Mother, he will be blessed by them.
By doing so we shall have performed the duty of mankind, and have done what ought to be done by a filial son, and by the living to the dead.
He had entered the dense fog on the hills and did not know where he was, when his mother leaned against the door-post and gnawed her fingers as if she would go in quest of him.

In the country of Ch‘u lived Lao Lai Tzŭ, who, when so old that he had lost nearly all his teeth, made every effort to rejoice and comfort his parents, constantly endeavouring to gladden their hearts.
He now reveres them, although dead, as if they were alive; and hopes they will condescend to dwell in his ancestral hall.
Taking up his rice and flesh, Ts‘ai returned home to his mother with the food; and in their joy they even forgot that the year was one of dearth.
His mother was in the habit of eating fresh fish at her meals, but winter coming, the ice bound up the rivers.
